newsitem.title: UK: Dollar recovers above 116 yen after Asian slide.
newsitem.headline: Dollar recovers above 116 yen after Asian slide.

text.p: The dollar recovered steam in early Europe to stand above 116.00-yen after stumbling briefly to 114.85-yen lows in Asian trade following a sharp rise in Japan's trade surplus.

Data released early on Monday showed Japan's overall customs-cleared trade surplus ballooned 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen ($7.2 billion) in April. Japan's sensitive surplus with the U.S also jumped 174.1 percent from a year earlier to 468.97 billion ($4.07 billion) yen.
But analysts said any impact on dollar/yen was likely to be short-lived.

"The numbers came in very close to expectations...The other interesting component is that exports were very strong but imports were not that weak," said Sean Shepley international economist CS First Boston.
At 0730 GMT the dollar was trading at 116.18 yen after slumping to lows of 114.85 yen in Asia immediately following the data and against 115.32/37 yen in late Europe on Friday.
Against the mark, the dollar was trading at 1.6940/45 marks, near half a pfennig up from early lows just below 1.6900 marks, and robust against 1.6900/10 marks in late Europe on Friday.
But turnover was stiffled as most Europe was on holidays.
Analysts, moreover, said dollar markets were likely to remain subdued ahead of the U.S Federal Open Market Committee Meeting (FOMC) on Tuesday.
Analysts said while it is unlikely that U.S rates will be moved, the market will be wary ahead of the policy meeting.

"I think markets are pretty much geared-up for no move, so if we were to see a surprise move, the dollar would see a significant rebound against the yen," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International.
